quotes.text: You can represent customers in your integration either as [customer-configured Account](https://docs.stripe.com/api/v2/core/accounts/create.md#v2_create_accounts-configuration-customer) objects or as [Customer](https://docs.stripe.com/api/customers/object.md) objects.
Set a lookup key for the price, then replace the following placeholders in the sample code:
Always keep sensitive information about your product inventory, such as price and availability, on your server to prevent customer manipulation from the client.
In a production environment, we recommend that you store this value alongside the authenticated user in your database.
After a successful payment and redirect to the success page, verify that the subscription status is `active` and grant your customer access to the products and features they subscribed to.

old_evidence.text: You can model customers in your integration either as customer-configured Account objects using the Accounts v2 API (recommended in most cases) or as Customer objects using the Customers v1 API.
Use `stripe.checkout.sessions.retrieve(session_id)` to get `customer_id`, then create portal session and redirect.

findings: Both captures identify https://docs.stripe.com/billing/quickstart as a Stripe Billing plus hosted Checkout sample, not a new integration product (old 6-10; new 5-17). The current source at 11-32 summarizes the old lookup-key, subscription Session, portal, five-event webhook, trial, anchor and tax path. Add the dated November capture and its central safety/state qualifications; retain the May capture separately.

The November text directs a recurring Price with lookup key (25-29), server-side inventory and Price ID selection (215-225), subscription mode (223-225), hosted Session URL redirect (211-241), and a portal session tied to the correct customer identity (57-63, 653-665). Neither the browser button nor a success-page message proves paid renewal or entitlement fulfillment.

New prose specifically says to verify active subscription status after successful payment and redirect before access grant (243-245); feature access also uses active-entitlements summary events and list API (33-37). The source should state this sample-specific condition without generalizing it to all asynchronous payment methods or replacing the broader webhook guidance in linked concepts.

The new capture is an amalgam of UI toggles, backend languages and examples. Adjacent duplicate success_url, subscription_data, customer/customer_account and portal calls appear in the flattened code (620-665; 1107-1129). It is not a single runnable source file or a proven compatible combination. The old raw labels itself a formatted React/Node UI capture (3-4), but its portal server excerpt retrieves the Checkout Session without the creation call (224-229). Current source's 'Full' runnable implication is too strong.
substantive_changes: New explicit product-plus-recurring-Price lookup key setup, server-authoritative inventory warning, and public success URL guidance are clearer than the May summary (new 23-31, 211-229; old 16-18, 56-62).
New active-status check before access grant and explicit webhook signing-secret environment instruction (new 243-249); current source omits the check and describes events only (21-26).

New customer-configured Account versus Customer identity alternatives, including customer_account portal code variants, are present (new 17, 636-665); the May raw already mentioned both objects (old 12), so Account support is not wholly new.

New payment-link no-code pointer (11-13), optional customization and many SDK/language snippets (65-209, 397-425, 533-1530) add detail and variant coverage, not proof that every example executes together.
historical_claims_to_preserve: May 12, 2026 raw's Accounts v2 'recommended in most cases' wording is dated to that capture (old 12); the November wording omits that recommendation (new 17). Omission does not prove a policy reversal.

May formatted React/Node sample and test-card details remain historical evidence (old 3-4, 80-90, 98-284). The November expanded multi-language capture must not retroactively replace their provenance.
Keep the older source's trial minimum and no-payment-method end behavior with new confirmation at 405-409; keep Stripe Tax activation qualification at 419-425.
conflicts: Current source 13 says 'Full Checkout-based subscription quickstart' and 'React client + Node.js/Express server'; November raw mixes HTML/React and Node/Ruby/Java/Python/PHP/Go/.NET with duplicate UI variants (65-209, 427-1530). Date and qualify the current source's coverage claim.

New quickstart 245 suggests active-status confirmation after successful payment/redirect; stripe-checkout concept's Fulfillment Pattern says webhook required and landing page optional, with asynchronous payment events. Preserve both by labeling the quickstart's active check as its example and warning that redirect alone is insufficient for general fulfillment.

The November flattened examples have duplicate keys and identity branches (620-665, 933-970, 1144-1185), while the May Node portal excerpt lacks an actual portal session creation call (224-229). Do not advertise either capture as a copy-paste runnable complete implementation.
unresolved_questions: Because the capture flattens hidden language and UI selections, it does not establish which code combinations the live interactive builder serves to a selected user.
No account, payment method eligibility, successful payment, bank receipt, or production execution was verified by this offline review.

answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/billing/quickstart, [[source-stripe-checkout-subscriptions-quickstart]] should describe a hosted Checkout subscription sample: a recurring Price lookup key resolves server-side, a subscription-mode Session redirects the customer, and a portal Session uses the correct customer identity (new 15-17, 25-29, 211-245, 653-665). The sample calls for webhook listening and active-status verification before access (new 243-245). The May capture already showed the core flow, both customer object choices and five events (old 8-12, 56-78); the current source at 11-32 summarizes it but lacks the new safety and fulfillment qualifications. The capture is documentation evidence, not proof of payment.
answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/billing/quickstart, [[source-stripe-checkout-subscriptions-quickstart]] needs a dated source update for explicit server-held price/availability data, portal identity variants and active-status fulfillment (new 17, 221, 243-245, 653-665). Added SDK languages, links, HTML fragments and test formatting are mostly presentation or variant expansion (new 65-209, 387-425, 427-1530); the old React/Node framing remains May 2026 history (old 3-4, 98-284). The old Accounts v2 recommendation (old 12) cannot be erased from its dated record merely because new 17 omits it. Flattened duplicate code and the old incomplete portal snippet preclude runnable-code claims; a success redirect alone does not settle asynchronous payment or entitlement state.
